transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. I'm here because I've, well, I've started planning my entire day around not using elevators. It's getting a bit ridiculous. I live on the fifth floor, so I'm taking five flights of stairs every day at home. I even turned down a training workshop recently because it was in a high-rise and I couldn't face it. And... I actually stopped visiting one of my older computer students because his building doesn't really have a good stair option. So, yeah, it's starting to get in the way of things.
When you think about using an elevator, what specifically goes through your mind? Are you worried something bad might happen, or is there another reason you avoid them?

Well, it's mostly the fear of getting stuck or falling. Like, logically, I know an elevator in a normal office block is probably safe. But when I look at those old doors in my apartment building, or even the ones at work... my mind just treats it like I’m about to get trapped in there, or like the whole thing is just going to drop. I mean, part of me knows that sounds a bit over the top, but that's exactly what goes through my head when I stand in front of one.
Do you experience similar intense fears or anxieties in other situations, like crowded places, open spaces, or social settings, or is this fear mostly limited to elevators?

No, not really. It's pretty much just limited to elevators. I don't have any issues with crowds or open spaces, and social settings are totally fine. I mean, I run training sessions for my job, so I'm around groups of people all the time without any problem. It really is just... elevators.

Have you ever had a sudden episode of intense fear or discomfort when you were near an elevator or when you tried to use one, where you felt symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, trembling, or a feeling like you were losing control?

Yeah, I do. It happens really fast. Like, as soon as I step toward an elevator, or even just hear the doors clunk open, my chest gets tight. My hands get sweaty, and... I just feel this immediate rush of panic. It hits me before I've even really had time to think it through. It's just an automatic reaction right then and there.
How long does that panic reaction usually last when you're near an elevator or hear the doors open?

I'm not exactly sure, I've never really timed it. It basically just lasts until I get away from the elevator. Like, once I turn around and head for the stairs instead, the feeling starts to fade almost immediately. So it's really just for those few minutes when I'm standing right there, and then my heart rate goes back to normal once I leave the area.
Does this panic reaction happen every time you're near an elevator, or are there times when you feel fine around them?

Yeah, it's pretty much every single time. I don't think there's ever a time I feel fine around them. Like I was saying a minute ago, the second I step toward one or hear those doors clunk open, that same rush of panic just hits me. My chest tightens up, my hands get sweaty... it's just an immediate reaction every time, before I can even think about it.
